purpose: Curated background papers and observed examples; separate from implemented processing references.

https://doi.org/10.3390/rs17020263.title: Radar observations of tidal-marsh inundation
https://doi.org/10.3390/rs17020263.description: Compares SAR inundation evidence with radiometric modeling and measured water levels at tidal marshes. Explains why vegetation and tide context matter for wetness interpretation.
https://doi.org/10.3390/rs17020263.review_scope: Publisher-indexed abstract, study-site description and author publication listing reviewed; direct publisher fetch was rate-limited
https://doi.org/10.3390/rs17020263.citation: Characterizing Tidal Marsh Inundation with Synthetic Aperture Radar, Radiometric Modeling, and In Situ Water Level Observations. Remote Sensing 17, 263.

https://deltax.jpl.nasa.gov/science/over.title: Delta-X: following water through Louisiana wetlands
https://deltax.jpl.nasa.gov/science/over.description: Explore radar observations and field measurements of tidal water movement in the Mississippi Delta. Delta-X uses multiple instruments and hydrodynamic models; P02 does not retrieve water level.
https://deltax.jpl.nasa.gov/science/over.review_scope: Primary abstract or documented case description reviewed

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2011.04.00.title: How radar responds to post-fire forest regrowth
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2011.04.00.scope: ALOS, Envisat and TerraSAR-X · other SAR missions
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2011.04.00.description: Compares SAR sensitivity to forest regrowth in Spain and Alaska. Supports careful reading of brightness trajectories; it does not make P03 a validated recovery or biomass estimator.
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2011.04.00.review_scope: Primary abstract or documented case description reviewed
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2011.04.00.citation: Sensitivity of SAR data to post-fire forest regrowth in Mediterranean and boreal forests. Remote Sensing of Environment 115, 2075–2085.

https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.title: A decade of fire scars and regrowth near Los Angeles
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.description: Compare radar observations of Angeles National Forest from 2010, 2017 and 2020. The mosaics illustrate changing vegetation after fires; their method differs from P03’s reference-normalized trajectory.
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.review_scope: Primary abstract or documented case description reviewed

https://doi.org/10.1186/s40623-015-0359-.title: Mapping the 2015 Gorkha earthquake with InSAR
https://doi.org/10.1186/s40623-015-0359-.description: Uses interferograms to investigate earthquake deformation and fault rupture in Nepal. Background for event-pair interpretation; detailed fault modeling is beyond P05.
https://doi.org/10.1186/s40623-015-0359-.review_scope: Primary abstract or documented case description reviewed
https://doi.org/10.1186/s40623-015-0359-.citation: Detailed crustal deformation and fault rupture of the 2015 Gorkha earthquake, Nepal, revealed from ScanSAR-based interferograms of ALOS-2. Earth, Planets and Space 67, 201.

https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.title: Venezuela earthquake displacement · June 2026
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.description: Published centimeter-scale map using June 13–25 and June 18–30 acquisitions. Compare regional patterns and read its geometry and Urgent Response context; no numerical ground-truth raster is supplied.
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.scope: NISAR · actual mission observations · multiple frames/tracks
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.review_scope: Acquisition dates, centimeter legend, viewing-geometry interpretation and urgent-response limitations checked against NASA and ASF documentation. No pixel-exact numerical comparison is claimed.

https://www.usgs.gov/publications/synthe.title: Combining radar brightness and coherence to map volcanic flows
https://www.usgs.gov/publications/synthe.description: Explains volcanic flow maps that combine cross-polarized amplitude changes with coherence. Relevant method background; P06’s GCOV scattering diary does not implement the full combined technique.
https://www.usgs.gov/publications/synthe.review_scope: Primary abstract or documented case description reviewed
https://www.usgs.gov/publications/synthe.citation: Synthetic aperture radar volcanic flow maps (SAR VFMs): A simple method for rapid identification and mapping of volcanic mass flows. DOI: 10.1007/s00445-022-01539-7.

https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/us-india-s.title: Watch NISAR track lava at Krasheninnikov
https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/us-india-s.description: NASA’s dated HH L-band sequence shows the evolving bright flow field. It uses an oblique 3D presentation, not a georeferenced lava classification; P06 measures changes since an observed baseline and cannot reconstruct older deposits automatically.
https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/us-india-s.review_scope: NASA article, SVS dataset metadata and dated video frames reviewed

https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4f48k1m.title: Mapping the flow of Antarctica’s ice sheet
https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4f48k1m.description: Explains continental ice-flow mapping from radar measurements. Its geographic ice velocities require processing beyond the radar-component offset rates displayed by P07.
https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4f48k1m.review_scope: Primary abstract or documented case description reviewed
https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4f48k1m.citation: Ice Flow of the Antarctic Ice Sheet. Science 333, 1427–1430. DOI: 10.1126/science.1208336.

https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.title: Antarctica’s moving ice: the published map
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.description: Explore the published Antarctic flow map and its spatial patterns. This illustrates the science context; P07 does not automatically reproduce a continental geographic velocity mosaic.
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-obs.review_scope: Primary abstract or documented case description reviewed

https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5661/.title: NISAR reveals flooding around Chókwè, Mozambique
https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5661/.description: Compare 5 and 17 January 2026 open-water views and HH/HV false-color composites. The Mozambique preset selects a smaller Chókwè study window. This is a NASA visualization, not a peer-reviewed paper or an independent accuracy mask; two dates show change but cannot establish recovery.
https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5661/.review_scope: Official NASA page, dated comparison images and public CMR acquisition metadata reviewed

https://doi.org/10.3390/rs18081172.title: Wheeler Marsh: inundation, depth and tide-gauge methods
https://doi.org/10.3390/rs18081172.scope: Historical PALSAR + elevation + field sensors · pre-NISAR observations
https://doi.org/10.3390/rs18081172.description: Extends the Wheeler study with HH/HV sigma-zero thresholds, a DEM and calibrated synthetic tide gauges. P02 now adapts the joint threshold rule after native conversion, but does not reproduce the filtering, depth, volume or published accuracy.
https://doi.org/10.3390/rs18081172.review_scope: Primary publication indexed full text or official agency page reviewed

https://eros.usgs.gov/doi-remote-sensing.title: Wheeler Marsh: USGS NISAR validation site
https://eros.usgs.gov/doi-remote-sensing.scope: Milford marsh sensor deployments for NISAR calibration/validation
https://eros.usgs.gov/doi-remote-sensing.description: Explains current water-level sensor deployments and shows historical PALSAR inundation maps. The illustrated 90% accuracy belongs to that earlier study, not this app or our 2026 NISAR test.
https://eros.usgs.gov/doi-remote-sensing.review_scope: Primary publication indexed full text or official agency page reviewed

https://www.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/st.title: Bridgeport tide gauge: context for the satellite dates
https://www.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/st.scope: Measured estuary water levels · separate from NISAR radar data
https://www.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/st.description: Check measured water levels at each acquisition time, rather than predictions alone. Levels use a stated vertical datum and do not measure water depth in each marsh pixel; local tidal lag and ponding still matter.
https://www.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/st.review_scope: Primary publication indexed full text or official agency page reviewed

https://science.iirs.gov.in/nisar-for-mo.title: NISAR glacier motion at Samudra Tapu and other glaciers
https://science.iirs.gov.in/nisar-for-mo.kind: IIRS science article · Malviya, Garg & Thakur, 2026
https://science.iirs.gov.in/nisar-for-mo.scope: Real NISAR GOFF study · exact pairs and band not specified
https://science.iirs.gov.in/nisar-for-mo.description: Publishes January 2026 Samudra Tapu maps alongside ITS_LIVE. P07 now offers a delivered-geometry horizontal estimate with zero vertical velocity, but this is not exact reproduction: the article omits pair IDs and conversion details. Compare support and assumptions as well as speed ranges.
https://science.iirs.gov.in/nisar-for-mo.review_scope: Complete official article, figure and cited data references reviewed; January-ending NASA GOFF subsets tested separately by viewing group
https://science.iirs.gov.in/nisar-for-mo.citation: Malviya, A., Garg, V. & Thakur, P. (2026). NISAR for Monitoring Glacier Motion. Sudoor Manthan, 3(4). DOI: 10.65456/iirs.2026.10.3.1.

https://nisar-docs.asf.alaska.edu/urgent.title: NISAR urgent-response observations
https://nisar-docs.asf.alaska.edu/urgent.description: Archive guidance for urgent-response observations and access. Check the delivered acquisition intervals and coverage before interpreting an event mosaic.
